A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PETS research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. v1 Appendices A-D correspond to v2 Appendices B-E; much of the earlier related-work discussion moves to v2 Appendix A.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original benchmark experiments on offline and online trajectory allocation, alongside simulations in Figures 2 and 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds confidence-guided comparisons, difficulty-bin sensitivity results, allocation timings, and reference-performance curves.

M1.justification: The offline OKG procedure, online greedy allocation, Gaussian-probit surrogate, and four-response difficulty grouping are retained. The expanded Section 4.1 explains components already documented in v1 Appendices B.3-B.4 and D.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GPQA-Diamond, AIME 2024, AIME 2025, BRUMO 2025, and HMMT February 2025 in offline and online settings, alongside the same simulations. The added analyses use existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds the DeepConf-based 'Conf. guided' comparator across all five datasets and five models in both Tables 2 and 3, substantially extending evaluation beyond uniform allocation and the online oracle. Figures 16-17 additionally include Pass@1 and MV@128 reference comparators. DeepConf was previously discussed but not evaluated as this allocation baseline.

E3.justification: Added experiments sweep oracle cluster counts of 2, 3, 5, and 8 and predictor bin counts of 2, 3, 4, and 5, measure allocation runtime, and evaluate single-sample and 128-sample voting references. The original benchmark protocol retains its 128-response pools and 64-trace finite proxy.

E4.justification: New Section 5.3 investigates sensitivity to oracle clustering and practical predictor discretization in Tables 4-5, and profiles allocation overhead in Table 6. These add direct evidence about parameter robustness and computational cost beyond the retained oracle comparisons and approximation simulations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 30 subsampling repetitions, retain the appendix tables formatted as mean (variance), and show the same 95% confidence intervals in Figure 2. No new repeated-run counts, seed controls, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Existing PETS, Uniform, and oracle table entries are retained, while substantial results are added for the new comparator and analyses. For example, Table 2 adds 10,652 traces for confidence-guided allocation on GPQA/Qwen3-4B; Table 6 reports 4.73 seconds for the online predictor versus 212.2 seconds for offline OKG. Tables 4-5 and Figures 16-17 add sensitivity and reference-performance results.

T1.justification: The self-consistency definitions, Bayes-optimal terminal rule, Theorem 4.1, Gaussian-probit approximation and concavity results, and asymptotic allocation derivations are retained. Appendix edits mainly add explanatory transitions and correct a proof cross-reference without changing mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and efficiency claims, including GPQA sampling reductions of up to 75% offline and 55% online. Added experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefining its scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly interprets bin-count sensitivity as evidence that coarse difficulty grouping suffices, and runtime measurements as support for practical streaming deployment. Figures 16-17 frame Pass@1 and MV@128 as lower and upper reference bounds. The limitation concerning systematically incorrect population majorities remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 6 newly documents the timing experiment's 30 training questions, four warm-up samples, and offline configuration of B=16 with 500 Monte Carlo samples. The added ablation captions specify clustering and bin-count configurations. Existing implementation details and code/data access links are retained.

R1.justification: The identifiable bibliography is unchanged, and most detailed related work is relocated. v2 adds a paragraph connecting crowdsourcing to uncertainty quantification and refines the main-text positioning, but introduces unresolved citation placeholders in Appendix A.

P1.justification: Focused revisions expand Section 4.1, polish proof prose, and replace the lengthy main-text related work with a summary plus Appendix A. Author affiliations and the equal-contribution footnote change, and an impact statement is added. Most scientific exposition retains its earlier wording and organization.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands result presentation: Tables 2-3 gain comparator rows, Tables 4-6 are new, and Figures 16-17 add multi-panel comparisons. Figure 1 is enlarged and several displays move. The original fifteen figures retain their content, and the full-result tables are renumbered as Tables 7-8.

improvement.justification: The evaluated confidence-guided baseline, discretization checks, and allocation timings strengthen empirical support beyond v1's uniform-baseline focus, while Section 4.1 becomes clearer. The gains are limited by sparse protocol details for the added experiments and new unresolved citations in Appendix A. The core method, theory, and earlier evidence remain intact.
